## About Me

I am a **Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) candidate in Statistics** at the **School of Mathematical Sciences, Adelaide University**. My research sits at the intersection of **statistics, data science, and ecology**, where I develop models that help translate complex environmental data into meaningful predictions.

Currently, I am working under the supervision of **A/Prof Ed Green**, **Dr John Maclean**, and **Dr Camille Buhl** on a project focused on **predicting pest outbreaks in Australia**. This work combines statistical and mathematical modelling to better understand ecological dynamics and improve forecasting accuracy.

My research is part of the *Analytics for the Australian Grains Industry (AAGI)* initiative,a five-year strategic partnership between **Adelaide University** and the **Grains Research and Development Corporation (GRDC)**. The project aims to harness advanced analytics to enhance the profitability, sustainability, and global competitiveness of the Australian grains sector.


I am passionate about **data-driven problem solving**, **statistical modelling**, **teaching**, and **knowledge sharing**. I enjoy working on problems where statistical thinking can create meaningful impact across disciplines.


## Inspiration

> “The best thing about being a statistician is that you get to play in everyone’s backyard.”  
> — John Tukey

This philosophy strongly shapes my academic journey. It has encouraged me to embrace **interdisciplinary research**, working across domains such as **agriculture, ecology, economics, and health**, where statistical thinking can provide valuable insight and solutions.

---

## Research Interests

 **Predictive Modelling**  
  Integrating mathematical and statistical models with field data to improve forecasting of ecological and agricultural pest outbreaks.

 **Time Series Analysis & Forecasting**  
  Classical, state-space, and structural time series models for economics, environmental, and industrial applications.

 **Computational Statistics & Data Science**  
  Statistical learning, predictive modelling, Bayesian methods, and reproducible research using **R**, **Python**, and **SAS**.
